result.overall: The Court allowed the judicial review application, set aside the Appeal Division's decision granting leave to appeal, and remitted the matter for reconsideration by a different member due to serious shortcomings including errors of law and lack of transparency in the Appeal Division's reasons.

themes.name: Leave to Appeal Requirements
themes.summary: The legal framework and statutory requirements for granting leave to appeal from the General Division to the Appeal Division under the Department of Employment and Social Development Act.

themes.name: Objective Medical Evidence Requirement
themes.summary: The necessity for claimants to provide objective medical evidence of disability existing on or before the Minimum Qualifying Period (MQP) to qualify for CPP disability benefits.

themes.name: Standard of Review and Reasonableness
themes.summary: The application of the reasonableness standard of review to the Appeal Division's decision, focusing on justification, transparency, and intelligibility as required by Vavilov.

themes.name: Transparency in Administrative Decisions
themes.summary: The importance of clear, transparent reasons in administrative decisions, especially in decisions granting leave to appeal, to enable understanding by parties and reviewing courts.

themes.name: Errors of Law by the Appeal Division
themes.summary: The Appeal Division's incorrect legal conclusions regarding the requirement for medical evidence to relate directly to the claimant's condition at the MQP and the existence of an error of law by the General Division.

arguments.quote: The AGC submits that the Appeal Division’s decision incorrectly found an error of law by the General Division
arguments.claim: The General Division made no error and the Appeal Division was incorrect to conclude otherwise
arguments.outcome_note: Court agreed the Appeal Division erred in law in finding an error by the General Division

arguments.quote: The AGC submits that a claimant must provide objective medical evidence to support a finding of disability on or before the MQP
arguments.claim: Objective medical evidence is required to obtain disability benefits under the CPP
arguments.outcome_note: Court agreed objective medical evidence is required

arguments.quote: The AGC submits that the Appeal Division erred in finding that Ms Angell’s appeal had a reasonable chance of success
arguments.claim: There is no arguable case on the objective medical evidence, so leave to appeal should have been refused
arguments.outcome_note: Court did not decide this issue, leaving it to the Appeal Division on redetermination

arguments.quote: The AGC requested that the application be granted without costs
arguments.outcome_note: Court agreed to grant without costs

holdings.statement: The Court allowed the judicial review application

holdings.quote: The decision of the Appeal Division will be set aside and the matter remitted back to the Appeal Division for a new decision on leave to appeal made by a different member
holdings.statement: The Appeal Division's decision granting leave to appeal is set aside and remitted for reconsideration by a different member

holdings.quote: The Court’s role right now is not to decide whether or not Ms Angell is entitled to disability benefits under the CPP
holdings.statement: The Court only reviews the decision to grant leave to appeal, not the merits of the disability claim

holdings.quote: The standard of review on this application is reasonableness
holdings.statement: Reasonableness is the presumed standard of review for administrative decisions, including this Appeal Division decision

holdings.quote: A decision will not be reasonable if the reasons, read in conjunction with the record, do not make it possible to understand the decision maker’s reasoning on a critical point
holdings.statement: Reasonableness requires transparent, intelligible, and justified reasons enabling understanding of the decision-maker's reasoning

holdings.quote: The Appeal Division was incorrect to conclude that the General Division erred in law on this issue
holdings.statement: The Appeal Division erred in law by wrongly finding the General Division made an error regarding medical evidence relating to the MQP

holdings.quote: To the extent that the Appeal Division concluded that no objective medical evidence is required, the Appeal Division was incorrect in law
holdings.statement: Objective medical evidence is required to support a disability claim under the CPP

holdings.quote: The Appeal Division’s reasons did not sufficiently communicate what it decided and why, did not identify for the parties a permitted ground for appeal on the merits, and will not enable the panel of the Appeal Division hearing the merits of the appeal to identify the legal error
holdings.statement: The Appeal Division's reasons lacked the required transparency and clarity

holdings.quote: The shortcomings in the Appeal Division’s decision are sufficiently serious to undermine both the reasoning and the outcome reached
holdings.statement: Serious shortcomings including errors of law and lack of transparency justify setting aside the decision

holdings.quote: I need not assess whether the Appeal Division’s reasons for granting leave to appeal sufficiently addressed subs. 58(2)
holdings.statement: The Court declined to decide whether the appeal had a reasonable chance of success under subs. 58(2) of the Act

rebuttals.quote: the courts do not require that the medical evidence relate directly to a claimant’s condition at the MQP and thereafter
rebuttals.point: Appeal Division found that medical evidence need not relate directly to the claimant's condition at the MQP
rebuttals.court_answer: The Court disagreed, holding that medical evidence must relate to the claimant's condition at or before the MQP to establish disability under CPP

rebuttals.quote: the Appeal Division concluded that no such objective medical evidence is required
rebuttals.point: Appeal Division concluded objective medical evidence is not required
rebuttals.court_answer: The Court held this was incorrect in law; objective medical evidence is required to support a disability claim

authorities.quote: The standard of review on this application is reasonableness: Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65
authorities.authority: Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65
authorities.why: Established the reasonableness standard of review and its application to administrative decisions

authorities.quote: A claimant must demonstrate entitlement to disability benefits by reason of a severe and prolonged disability existing prior to the MQP: Brennan v Attorney General of Canada, 2011 FCA 318
authorities.authority: Brennan v Attorney General of Canada, 2011 FCA 318
authorities.why: Confirmed requirement that disability must exist on or before MQP and continuously thereafter

authorities.quote: A claimant must provide objective medical evidence to support a finding of disability on or before the MQP: Gholipour v Canada (Attorney General), 2017 FCA 99
authorities.why: Confirmed necessity of objective medical evidence to support disability claim

authorities.quote: Paragraph 68(1)(a) of the Canada Pension Plan Regulations requires a report of any physical or mental disability including nature, extent and prognosis
authorities.authority: Canada Pension Plan Regulations, CRC, c 385, para 68(1)(a)
authorities.why: Regulatory requirement for medical reports supporting disability claims

authorities.quote: Transparency is a hallmark of administrative decision-making: Vavilov, at para 15
authorities.authority: Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65
authorities.why: Emphasized transparency as essential to reasonableness in administrative decisions

authorities.quote: Justification and intelligibility are present when the basis for a decision has been given and is understandable: Vancouver Airport Authority v PSAC, 2010 FCA 158
authorities.authority: Vancouver Airport Authority v PSAC, 2010 FCA 158
authorities.why: Clarified requirements for justification, intelligibility, and transparency in administrative decisions

authorities.quote: Court of Appeal for Ontario set aside a decision for lack of transparency: Romania v Boros, 2020 ONCA 216
authorities.why: Illustrated importance of transparency in administrative decision-making

left_open.quote: The AGC submitted that Ms Angell did not have a reasonable chance of success on the merits of the appeal
left_open.issue: Whether Ms Angell had a reasonable chance of success on the merits of the appeal under subs. 58(2) of the Department of Employment and Social Development Act
left_open.reason: The Court declined to address this issue, leaving it to the Appeal Division on redetermination
